overview: This House resolution set the ground rules for debating three measures in March 2025. It allowed the House to consider H.J. Res. 25, which would use the Congressional Review Act to overturn an Internal Revenue Service rule requiring certain brokers of digital assets such as cryptocurrency to report sales proceeds; H.R. 1156, which would give the government more time to pursue fraud in pandemic-era unemployment programs; and H.R. 1968, a stopgap spending bill to fund the government for the rest of the 2025 budget year. Each got one hour of debate and limited chances to change it. It also said that the remaining days of the 2025 session would not count toward the deadline under the National Emergencies Act for the House to vote on a resolution ending a national emergency the President declared on February 1, 2025. On September 16, 2025, another House resolution, H. Res. 707, amended it.
for: Supporters say the resolution let the House move quickly on government funding and other priorities without being sidetracked by procedural maneuvers.
against: Critics say it limited debate and amendments on major bills and, by stopping the calendar clock, kept the House from being forced to vote on ending a presidential emergency declaration.
